
## BONUS: `if __name__ == 'main'`

If you head to the folder in sample_code, you may notice a funny line:

::: {.codewindow .python}
b_simple_one_step_model_vidigi.py
```{.python code-line-style="dim:1-3,focus:4,dim:5-8" code-line-style-preset="emphasis"}
class Model:
    ...

if __name__ == "__main__":
    my_params = Param()
    my_model = Model(my_params)
    my_model.run_model()
    ...
```
:::

## BONUS: `if __name__ == 'main'` - explanation

`if __name__ == 'main':` simply means [**'only run the code in this block if you are running the original file'**]{style="color:yellow"}

When you run the file (script) in the terminal or the interactive window, the code in this block will run (execute).

::: {.fragment}
HOWEVER, if you import pieces of that code into another file, it *won't* run the bit in the `if __name__ == 'main':` block.
:::


::: {.value-box fragment="fade-in" icon="fa-solid fa-lightbulb" icon-position="left" align="center" color="bg-green"}
This is really useful if we want to reuse our `Param` and `Model` classes somewhere else, like in a web app, so we'll be getting in the habit of doing this.
:::
